fix_prompts.problem: Jerry has a validated FAIL verdict: -$1121.59 total P&L across 121 trades, 36.4% win rate, 0.951 profit factor, negative Sharpe (-0.008), 14.0% max drawdown, and -$9.27 expectancy per trade.
fix_prompts.root_cause: Norman's validation shows a sufficiently large sample with negative expectancy and profit factor below 1.0. This is not a data-size problem or normal variance; Jerry's current strategy is structurally unfit for capital.
fix_prompts.strategic_diagnosis: The bleeding from Jerry is not accidental. One hundred twenty-one trades are enough to convict a negative-expectancy machine, and the 0.951 profit factor confirms it has no margin for friction or error. Keep it parked and force a full strategy redesign under paper validation before a single dollar returns.
fix_prompts.fix_prompt: Audit and harden the Jerry trading system. First locate Jerry's strategy, execution configuration, risk settings, and trade-log pipeline under /root/.openclaw/workspace and the relevant agent directory; use rg to identify the exact files before editing. Preserve the existing production configuration, explicitly keep Jerry disabled/parked, and create a versioned paper-only replacement configuration that addresses the validated failure: require positive expected value after fees, add a hard daily loss limit, cap consecutive-loss exposure, require setup-quality filters, and log setup tag, entry, stop, initial dollar risk, realized P&L, fees, slippage, and exit reason for every closed trade. Add a validation script or report that calculates win rate, profit factor, expectancy, Sharpe, max drawdown, and sample count from the new logs, and blocks any request to enable live capital until at least 50 paper trades show profit factor above 1.10 and positive expectancy after costs. Verify by running the test suite or targeted checks, confirm the service remains disabled, and report the exact files changed plus the command used to generate the validation report.
fix_prompts.estimated_impact: Prevents further deployment of a process losing an average $9.27 per trade and creates a measurable gate before capital can be reintroduced.
